analyses.extracted_text:
Group axioms
A group is a triplet \\(G, \, \cdot, \, e\\) satisfying:
(1) Closure: For all a, b \\(\in G, \, a \, \cdot \, b \\in G\\)
(2) Associativity: For all a, b, c \\(\in G, \, a \, \cdot \, (b \, \cdot \, c) \\equiv \, (a \, \cdot \, b) \, \cdot \, c\\)
(3) Identity: For all a \\(\in G, \, a \, e \, 	ext{= \,} e \, a \, 	ext{= \,} a\\)
(4) Inverse: For all a \\(\in G, \, 	ext{there exists} \, b \\(\in G, \, 	ext{such that} \, a \, \cdot \, b \, 	ext{= \,} b \, \cdot \, a \, 	ext{= \,} e\\)

analyses.extracted_text:
Symmetries:
A transformation that preserves
distances and the object

Properties:
\left(\begin{array}{l}
(1) \text{ Composition of symmetries is a symmetry.} \\
(2) \text{ Composition of symmetries is associative.} \\
(3) \text{ Not doing anything is a symmetry. } \quad (\text{Identity}) \\
(4) \text{ We can undo symmetries.}
\end{array}\right)
analyses.visual_description: This slide defines symmetries as transformations preserving distances and the object itself. It lists four key properties of symmetries: closure under composition, associativity of composition, existence of an identity symmetry (doing nothing), and existence of inverses (undoing symmetries). The properties are enclosed in a blue rectangular box with the word 'Properties:' in cyan and the identity property highlighted in yellow.
analyses.alignment_note: The spoken transcript likely explains the concept of symmetries and their fundamental properties as listed on the slide, emphasizing the preservation of distances and the object, and the algebraic structure of symmetries.
